title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the first page (numbered 1) of a 38-page sub-dossier. The previous page gives its title as roughly: 'Generalities on actions of Galois groups on profinite completions of fundamental groupoids of complex algebraic varieties'. The page sets up the framework.

(i) Base field. K is a subfield of C. The model cases are Q, a number field, and Q-bar (the algebraic closure of Q inside C). The main interest is K of finite type over Q. Q-bar is described as a 'limit' case of these (a direct limit of finitely generated fields). Grothendieck says it is useful 'so as not to be bothered by the roots of unity': over Q-bar the cyclotomic character, and with it the Tate twists, become invisible.

(ii) Objects. The objects are schemes X of finite type over K, together with their analytic spaces X(C). Since only 'topological' invariants matter, morphisms X' -> X that are universal homeomorphisms are treated as isomorphisms. In particular nilpotents are ignored and a surjective closed immersion counts as an isomorphism. Over C this is consistent on both sides:
- A universal homeomorphism of finite-type C-schemes is finite, radicial and surjective. It therefore induces a bijective, proper (hence closed) continuous map X'(C) -> X(C), that is, a homeomorphism.
- On the étale side, the topological invariance of the étale site (SGA1 IX 4.10; SGA4 VIII 1.1) gives the same conclusion.

(iii) Language. X is viewed as the analytic, or even merely topological, space X(C) endowed with an extra 'structure of algebraic variety over K'. This structure consists of the Zariski topology, the sheaf of K-polynomial functions, and so on. By abuse, X is written for X(C).

(iv) Fundamental groupoids. On X one distinguishes the topological fundamental groupoid Π_1(X), whose objects are all points of X(C), and its profinite completion Π̂_1(X). The latter can be defined directly in terms of the C-scheme X: it is the étale fundamental groupoid with the C-points as base points. There is an 'inclusion' functor Π_1 -> Π̂_1, written down on the next page.

The next page goes on to:
- identify π_1^et(X_C, x) with the profinite completion of π_1^top (Riemann existence theorem, SGA1 XII);
- describe path sets Hom(x,y) as bitorsors obtained by extension of the operator groups;
- introduce Π_K = Aut_{K-alg}(C), with the aim of letting Aut(C/K) act on Π̂_1(X) for X defined over K.

The overall problem is to set up the outer, or groupoid-level, Galois action on profinite fundamental groupoids of varieties over K. This is the foundation of the 'Galois action on Teichmüller' program, i.e. Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory and anabelian geometry.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The claim that universal homeomorphisms induce homeomorphisms on X(C), and leave Π_1 and Π̂_1 unchanged, is correct in characteristic 0.

The remark that Q-bar avoids being 'bothered by roots of unity' is heuristic and left unexplained. Presumably it means that Gal(C/Q-bar), or Aut(C/Q-bar), acts trivially on μ_∞, so the cyclotomic twists disappear. Note that Aut(C/Q-bar) still acts nontrivially on X(C), i.e. on the objects of the groupoid.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a foundational set-up page whose content is standard: topological invariance, the profinite completion of π_1 via SGA1, and finitely generated base fields. The only mildly distinctive feature, the plan to use Aut(C/K) acting on groupoids with all complex points as base points, is only announced here and developed on the following pages.
